statements.statement: The CNN method learns the entire processing pipeline to steer an automobile directly from raw sensor data, generating steering commands from a single front-facing center camera image.

ChauffeurNet employs an RNN architecture that takes mid-level input representations and outputs driving trajectories for control, incorporating components such as FeatureNet and AgentRNN, with recurrent feedback between iterations.
The RNN approach benefits from mid-level representations that enable training on both real and simulated data and facilitate closed-loop simulation testing before real deployment.
This comparison highlights the architectural and input representation differences between end-to-end CNN and RNN methods in autonomous driving control.
